authority.title: Who owns each fact
authority.caption: Application composition borrows public ports. Dashed boundaries separate ownership. P3 uses public P1 grants/results; none of the three libraries gains permission to copy sibling storage.

commit.title: The two orders of revision and intent
commit.caption: Both schedules use P1’s protected authority: revision-first rejects the old quote; intent-first rejects revision. Client timestamps and response order do not decide the winner.

effect.title: A possible external effect stays possible
effect.caption: Conceptual knowledge states, not the exact storage enum. A prior reservation stays possible after a lookup miss. In the illustrated takeover, P1 retains terminal uncertainty even when the old call later applies.

lease.title: A lease check after the lock wait
lease.caption: Illustrative order, not measured durations. The lease can expire during the lock wait, so the guarded decision uses fresh database time afterward. This local write fence does not cancel a prior supplier request.

feedcommit.title: Feed sequence follows visible commit order
feedcommit.caption: Live result, scoped head and event commit together under shared work admission. The global precommit-sequence counterexample is an unimplemented alternative. adopted_history has upgrade adoption order, not reconstructed original commit order.

intake.title: Durable input before dispatched generation
intake.caption: The opt-in native adapter accepts input before dispatched generation. One accepted input may have multiple generation/response identities; neither repeat-commit safety nor the two-handle SDK lifecycle proves exactly-once generation or playback.

context.title: Rehydrate without inventing an atomic snapshot
context.caption: P2 and public P1 observations occur at different times. The final permission check restricts disclosure but does not make the earlier reads a cross-store atomic transaction.

outbound.title: Reserve permission before carrier I O
outbound.caption: Reservation commits local permission before carrier I/O and shares admission with callback evidence. Any retained callback vetoes a new reservation; neither later callback nor revocation retracts an already admitted possible call.

auth.title: Authenticate twice for two different questions
auth.caption: After local call admission, the cheap pass authenticates signed bytes before SQL but cannot establish current freshness. Protected intake checks freshness again with database time after the shared admission lock.

delegation.title: Acceptance issuance result and action
delegation.caption: These are separate authority gates. The fresh running-grant read is a preflight, not a remote cancellation fence. Original v1 action and newer policy delivery facades have distinct support; the flow grants no automatic version compatibility.

feed.title: Scan progress is not the terminal watermark
feed.caption: This is a retained eight-event window, not one returned processing page. Terminally ACKed rows are excluded from discovery; later useful events can finish while an earlier unknown holds the contiguous watermark behind the gap.

facts.title: Valid bytes can still be unsupported facts
facts.caption: Conceptual gates across supported paths, not an implemented v2/v3 action pipeline. Both policy verifiers reject unsupported facts before returning expiry; v1 and v2 have different witness and uncertainty rules.

singleflight.title: Shared scan and independent observers
singleflight.caption: One published scan can serve two observers. Canceling the first does not cancel the second; losing the last observer abandons interest while actual ownership remains until settled.

webrtc.title: Signaling and media use different paths
webrtc.caption: Protocol overview. A control connection is not proof of a working media path. TURN relays a path; it does not become application consent or a durable inbox.

pipeline.title: Where a voice answer can pause
pipeline.caption: Conceptual cascaded pipeline for the opt-in P2/joined admission path, not measured latency or every LiveKit model mode. Streaming stages can overlap; arbitrary duration sums are not an observed end-to-end delay.

triage.title: Start with the missing observation
triage.caption: A diagnostic decision guide. Follow the evidence for the failing layer instead of treating every silence, delay or missing receipt as one retryable error.

lifetime.title: One timeout and three remaining lifetimes
lifetime.caption: Composite example for retained loopback/media owners, not every slot in the repo. Ordinal stages are not measurements. Each slot releases when its own protected actual resource settles; some require writer closure.

nats.title: Three acknowledgments with different meanings
nats.caption: Hypothetical integration: configured stream storage acceptance, consumer progress and an application receipt are distinct. Quorum acknowledgment does not alone establish per-write filesystem sync.

planes.title: LiveKit transport bus and application authority
planes.caption: Inspected upstream source snapshots show Redis/local server construction and a NATS-capable PSRPC library. They are separate from the POC image, and establish no private Cloud topology or NATS service here.
